title.narrative: Life-saving response through the provision of emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items to Returnees from Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtSince the onset of the Sudan conflict in April 2023, an estimated 892,139 people have crossed into South Sudan (UNHCR/IOM dashboard, 12 December 2024). The influx of arrivals from Sudan has created additional strain on the humanitarian response and overwhelmed coping capacities in host communities. According to the United Nations (UN) Contingency Plan for the Sudan Crisis 2025, worst-case scenario, approximately 358,830 people are projected to cross into South Sudan in the first 90 days of 2025, via six main entry points and twelve secondary crossing points in Upper Nile, Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Abyei, and Western Bahr el Ghazal. On the hand, the most likely scenario estimates that 2,658 people will cross the border entry points daily, bringing the total in the first 90 days to 239,220 arrivals.ltbrgtAccording to the head count conducted by ACTED in December 2024, 86 per cent of the people crossing the Sudan-South Sudan border are returnees with the majority being women and children who make up 82 per cent of the population. The individuals arriving are in dire need of health, WASH, child protection, and Shelter/NFI assistance. Should the worst-case scenario play out, the current humanitarian capacity remains insufficient to respond to the expected influx of people adequately.ltbrgtFollowing the expansion of conflict in Sudan to Sudanese states bordering South Sudan and with fears of increased number of people crossing into South Sudan this project, with funding from the South Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SSHF), and through the IOM Core Pipeline, will provide emergency shelter and NFI assistance to 17,000 vulnerable returnees in Kirr Adem (Aweil North) and Majokyinthiou (Aweil East). It is worth noting that the intervention will be initiated upon activation of the Sudan crisis triggers.ltbrgtThe IOM Core Pipeline is a centrally managed supply mechanism that plays a crucial role in South Sudan’s SNFI sector’s emergency preparedness and response by ensuring that SNFI Cluster response partners have ready access to prepositioned response supplies at strategically positioned warehouse hubs. Furthermore, the Core Pipeline ensures standardization of supplies and cost efficiency through economies of scale and facilitates timely and coordinated responses.ltbgt IOM will procure and preposition 2,833 emergency SNFI kits at its Bentiu and Wau warehouses, ensuring access for SNFI Cluster partners operating in Kirr Adem and Majokyinthioult/bgt. ltbgtIn addition, the project will conduct post distribution monitoring aimed at assessing the level of satisfaction among the beneficiaries on the SNFI provided and how they were delivered.lt/bgt The kits are comprised of plastic sheets, rubber rope, blankets, mosquito nets and sleeping mats. The kit composition will enable the returnee households to quickly construct emergency shelters, access to bedding and ensure prevention of malaria and any other cold related diseases such as pneumonia especially among the children under five. The project aims to assist 2,833 returnee households comprised of an estimated 17,000 individuals which will be selected based on the level vulnerability as determined by the SNFI cluster standardized toolsltbrgtlt/pgt
